problem: The number of randomly chosen codewords is printed as "2nR", which reads as 2 × n × R. The random-coding proof uses 2^(nR) codewords, i.e. 2 raised to the power nR, to get rate R = (log₂ M)/n with M = 2^(nR). A student reading 2nR would get a completely wrong rate.
fix: Choose 2<sup>nR</sup> codewords independently from the input distribution that achieves C.

problem: The answer is corrupted: "every rate R e → 0 as n → ∞" has lost the condition R < C and the symbol P<sub>e</sub>, so the statement is meaningless and, as printed, wrong.
fix: answer: For a DMC with capacity C, every rate R < C has some code with P<sub>e</sub> → 0 as n → ∞; every rate R > C has P<sub>e</sub> bounded away from 0.

where: Section 2, coding gain formula and the 10 dB / 7 dB example
problem: The formula needs the linear (power-ratio) values of Eb/N0, but the example quotes 10 dB and 7 dB. A student who substitutes 10 and 7 directly into the formula gets 10 log₁₀(10/7) = 1.55 dB, not the 3 dB stated.
fix: Add after the formula: convert dB to linear first, Eb/N0 = 10^(dB/10). So 10 dB → 10 and 7 dB → 5.01, and 10 log₁₀(10/5.01) = 3.0 dB, which is just the difference of the two dB values.
